Truf is a popular Indonesian trick-taking game with bidding, classified under the Exact Bidding group. The name is probably derived from the Dutch word troef (trump), reflecting historical Dutch influence in Indonesia. Players bid by placing a card from hand face down to propose trump suit and number of tricks; trumps are played face down and revealed only after each trick. The documented rules draw on information from Indonesian contributors Riza Purwo Nugroho, David Nugraha and Hamdanil Rasyid. The game is played in Indonesia and among Indonesian communities abroad (e.g. Singapore, California).
52 cards (4 players) or 39 (3 players, remove 1 black suit). 13 each.
